source.author: ov
source.text: res latuit, priscique manent imitamina facti; aera deae comites raucaque terga movent, cymbala pro galeis, pro scutis tympana pulsant; tibia dat Phrygios, ut dedit ante, modos.
source.text_original: res latuit, priscique manent imitamina facti; / aera deae comites raucaque terga movent, / cymbala pro galeis, pro scutis tympana pulsant; / tibia dat Phrygios, ut dedit ante, modos.'
source.text_english: The matter was concealed, and there remain imitations of the ancient deed; the goddess’s attendants move bronze and their hoarse backs, beating cymbals for helmets and drums for shields; the flute gives Phrygian tunes, as it did before.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: nam quia tum Corybautes galearum tinnitibus et scutorum pulsibus uagitum pueri texerant , nunc imago rei refertur in sacris, sed pro galeis cymbala, pro scutis tympana feriuntur, ne puerum uagientem Saturnus exaudiat.
reuse.text_original: nam quia tum Corybautes galearum tinnitibus et scutorum pulsibus uagitum pueri texerant , nunc imago rei refertur in sacris, sed pro galeis cymbala, pro scutis tympana feriuntur, ne puerum uagientem Saturnus exaudiat.
reuse.text_english: For because then the Corybantes had covered the baby’s crying with the ringing of helmets and the beating of shields, now the image of that event is reproduced in the rites, but cymbals are struck in place of helmets and drums in place of shields, so that Saturn may not hear the crying child.
